AFIR and ISO 15118-20: what changes on 1 January 2027 | VOOL
From 1 January 2027 newly installed AC charging points in the EU must support ISO 15118-20. The new VOOL Charger does, and existing VOOL chargers can be upgraded.
Chargers installed from 1 January 2027 need ISO 15118-20. VOOL is ready.
The new VOOL Charger supports ISO 15118-2, ISO 15118-20 and Plug & Charge. It ships from mid-December 2026. Chargers you already have can be upgraded.
Since 8 January 2026: newly installed or renovated publicly accessible AC charging points must support EN ISO 15118-2.
From 1 January 2027: newly installed or renovated AC (Mode 3) charging points must support EN ISO 15118-20. This covers public and private charging points.
Existing chargers stay as they are. The rule applies to new installations and renovations, not to chargers installed before the deadline.
Public charging points must also offer ad hoc payment without a contract and show the price before charging starts. For AC, a QR code payment page is enough.

The rules come from the EU’s Alternative Fuels Infrastructure Regulation (AFIR) and its delegated regulation (EU) 2025/656. The Commission is still publishing guidance on the details, so check the current text before a tender.
Both versions from the first day, so the charger meets the 2026 and the 2027 requirements.
The car identifies itself when it is plugged in. No app or card needed to start.
Bidirectional charging arrives as a firmware update in the first quarter of 2027.

Can I still install the current VOOL charger in December 2026?
Yes. The ISO 15118-20 requirement applies to charging points installed or renovated from 1 January 2027.
Do I have to replace chargers that are already installed?
No. Chargers installed before the deadline can stay. An upgrade is your choice.
Does the rule apply to a private home?
From 1 January 2027 it covers newly installed private AC charging points too.
